name: Jucam
overview: Jucam is a male figure mentioned uniquely as the son of Ezer in the Septuagint version of Genesis 36:27, specifically in Rahlfs' edition. This name does not appear in the traditional Hebrew Masoretic Text, highlighting a textual variant found in the Greek translation of the Old Testament. No tribal affiliation or additional background information is provided for Jucam.
namesAndTitles: The name 'Jucam' is presented as a proper name in the Septuagint but lacks a recorded meaning or divine origin within the biblical text. There are no further titles or meanings attached to this name in the given data.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Jucam explicitly as the son of Ezer, as noted in Genesis 36:27 according to the Septuagint. Beyond this paternal relationship, no other family connections or genealogical details are recorded for Jucam.
scriptureSignificance: Jucam's significance lies primarily in his inclusion within the genealogical records of Genesis 36, which trace the descendants of Esau. His mention in the Septuagint but absence from the Hebrew text underscores the importance of textual traditions in biblical studies. While not a central biblical character, Jucam contributes to the broader understanding of Esau's lineage as preserved in the Greek Old Testament.
